neutrophils and activated macrophages control mucosal immunity by proteolytic cleavage of antileukopeptidase.
neutrophil elastases and gelatinase B (MMP-9) control mucosal immunity by proteolytic cleavage of antileukopeptide.

the proteolytic regulation of the innate immune system, in particular the regulation of antileukocyte peptidases by neutrophils and macrophages.
the role of antileukoprotenase in the regulation of the mucosal immune system, in particular in the lung.
the proteolytic regulation of antileukoproterinase by neutrophils and macrophages and the consequences of this process for the control of inflammation in mucosal surfaces.

neutrophils and activated macrophages are able to control mucosal immune reactions by proteolysis.

the proteolytic activity of neutrophil-derived elastase and macrophage-derived gelatinase B/MMP-9, which are the most abundant and active proteases present in the airway lumen of patients with bronchiectasis (and other chronic inflammatory lung diseases), can be controlled by antileukoprotease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteolytic activity of neutrophils is controlled by antileukoprotease.
the proteolytic regulation of antileuko- proteinase by neutrophils and macrophages is an important component of the mucosal innate immune defense.

The main takeaway from our work is that
antileukoproteinas is a target for proteolysis by neutrophil and macrophage proteases and that proteolytic cleavage of antileukoprotenase is a key event in the regulation of the inflammatory process.

antileukopproteinase is a novel target for proteolytic regulation in the airways and that the cleavage of antileukoproreteinase by neutrophil-derived enzymes is an important mechanism to control local mucosal immunity.
